prototype_hypothesis: lvx_list_item_create(parent) -> object; lvx_list_item_init(object, optional_icon, primary_text, secondary_text, badge_value, style, trailing_kind); lvx_list_item_update(object, icon_resource, primary_text, secondary_text, badge_value, compact_flag)

ownership_analysis: The returned list item is an LVGL/LVX object parented into the page object tree. Static evidence strongly suggests recursive parent teardown owns it, but the delete function, owner thread, and safe mutation phase have not yet been proved. Public application code must never retain this pointer; only the exact-target backend may hold it.
unsafe_assumptions: parameter 6/7 enum meanings are only partially inferred from common assets and callsites
construct/update calls are not yet device-probed on a synthetic page
the page/UI owner thread and recursive destruction contract remain unresolved
no callable should be generated while status remains STATIC_RECOVERED/restricted
recommended_probe: On a disposable synthetic native page, call create+init on the page-owned root, render one primary/secondary row with trailing_kind=3 (forward icon), update only copied strings, then close the page and verify recursive teardown with allocator/UI diagnostics.
